title: Stone Game VIII
summary: Alice and Bob play a game with stones.
statement: Alice and Bob play a game with stones. Alice starts. They remove a segment of stones, add their value to their score, and place a new stone with that value. The game ends when one stone remains. Alice aims to maximize the score difference, while Bob aims to minimize it. Given stone values, determine the score difference if both play optimally.
constraints: A move replaces at least the first two stones by their sum and awards that sum to the current player.
hints: Every merged leading stone equals a prefix sum of the original array.
Let best represent the optimal advantage after the game has reached a given prefix.
Scan prefix endpoints backward using best = max(best, prefix[i] - best).
At each state the player either preserves the later optimal choice or takes prefix i and leaves the opponent the stored advantage; backward induction proves the recurrence.

tests.explanation: Optimal play gives Alice a final score advantage of five.
Considering every legal prefix through the suffix recurrence gives thirteen.
